validity.recommendation: Add PNGRB (current + 2016) + Indian Infrastructure refs to Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Capacity/Length/Owner [ref] cells. No value change needed -- Status, Length, Capacity, Owner all check out against a primary regulator.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/STATUS/SPEC/DUPLICATE, checked independently of gem.wiki's own citations (mined for leads only). PNGRB's current line-wise register (PNGRB MIS REPORT: NGPL, month of MAY 2026, printed p.2 'PHYSICAL PROGRESS REPORT OF NATURAL GAS PIPELINE') lists this exact pipeline as S.No.20 under the OPERATIONAL COMMON CARRIER PIPELINE section: Entity GAIL, Authorisation Date 13.12.2010, Authorised Length 455 km, Authorised Capacity 35.0 MMSCMD, Design/Determined Capacity 13.2 MMSCMD, Operating Length 440 km, states passing through 'HR, RJ & DL'. url_verifier FAILs its content check on this URL (200 but 'missing expected') because it is a real zip-deflated PDF -- the documented large/compressed-PDF false negative -- so I downloaded it and ran `pdftotext -layout`, which resolves the row cleanly (grep -n 'chainsa' hit line 101 with the full row). This is a PRIMARY REGULATORY SOURCE (PNGRB, India's pipeline regulator), which is HIGH tier on its own per confidence_tiers.md even without a second source. GEM's Status=operating matches (the pipeline sits in the OPERATIONAL section, not PARTIALLY COMMISSIONED or UNDER CONSTRUCTION). GEM's Owner1=GAIL (India) Ltd 100% matches the Entity column exactly. GEM's Capacity=35.00 MMSCMD matches the AUTHORISED capacity column exactly (not the lower 13.2 MMSCMD Design/Determined figure) -- consistent with the orchestrator's finding that GEM's India gas Capacity field tracks PNGRB's authorised MMSCMD directly. GEM's LengthKnown=455.00 km matches the Authorised Length column exactly (Operating Length this month is 440 km, i.e. ~97% built-out, no length still shown as 'Under Construction' -- the residual 15 km gap is unexplained in the report but is not large enough to contest the 455 km authorised/nameplate figure GEM records). I then pulled the ORIGINAL 2016 PNGRB report that gem.wiki itself cites (http://www.pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/NGPL-Operating-15012016.pdf, cite_note-pngrb-1 on the wiki page) as a second, decade-earlier edition of the same regulator's register: it lists the pipeline as S.No.8 'Chhainsa-Jhajjar-Hissar' (note the historical 'Chhainsa' spelling with two h's -- this, not a typo in my search, is why the url_verifier substring check on 'Chainsa' fails on both PNGRB PDFs), Length 455.0 km, Capacity 35.000 MMSCMD, Authorization date 13.12.2010 -- all identical to the 2026 edition -- with a footnote that only 265.02 of 455 km was built at the time (189.98 km under construction). This confirms the pipeline is a real, decade-tracked regulatory asset that was built out over roughly 2011-2024ish, not a phantom or a GEM-only entity. A third, independent (non-regulatory) source, the trade publication Indian Infrastructure (https://indianinfrastructure.com/2024/07/30/growing-coverage-strategies-for-building-a-unified-gas-grid/, verified OK by url_verifier on both 'Chainsa-Jhajjar-Hissar' and '48 per cent'), independently names 'Chainsa-Jhajjar-Hissar natural gas pipeline (CJHPL) ... operating at 48 per cent capacity utilisation' as of mid-2024 -- confirming both existence and operating status from a source with no connection to PNGRB or GEM. CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType=transmission is correct -- PNGRB classifies it as a 'common carrier' trunk/transmission network (the same category as HVJ, East-West, KG Basin, etc. in the same table), not a gathering or process line. DUPLICATE CHECK against the 35-pipeline India-gas roster: no overlap. It is NOT part of the HVJ/GREP/DVPL combined system (PNGRB reports that as one separate multi-row entry, S.No.3-4, corresponding to GEM's P0925/P0919/P3298/P3297/P3299 family) and does not overlap Dadri-Bawana-Nangal (P0916, a different authorised system, S.No.21 in the current report) or Dadri-Panipat (P0917, S.No.10). A GAIL capacity-declaration table (gailebank.gail.co.in/Schedule1/12.html, read for leads only, not cited -- it is a GAIL corporate portal, effectively a company self-report with no independent verification value) shows the Chhainsa hub feeding FOUR separately-named legs (Chainsa-Sakatpur, Chainsa-Manesar, Chainsa-Hisar, Chainsa-Neemrana) -- consistent with GEM's single P0912 row representing the authorised 455 km Chainsa-...-Hissar trunk/system as PNGRB itself aggregates it, not a sign that any leg is separately duplicated elsewhere in the roster. Net: existence, status, classification, length, capacity and owner are all solidly confirmed; no reason to doubt this row.

validity.recommendation: No field change -- StartLocation/EndLocation/Start-EndState are correct as recorded. Add a ResearcherNotes line that PNGRB's own register lists the pipeline as transiting Rajasthan and Delhi in addition to its Haryana endpoints, since GEM's schema has no 'transit states' field to capture that.
validity.researcher_notes: Checked the endpoint geography specifically because PNGRB's current register lists 'States Passing Through' as 'HR, RJ & DL' (Haryana, Rajasthan, Delhi) for this pipeline, while GEM records StartState/Province=Haryana and EndState/Province=Haryana for both ends -- worth checking this wasn't a misattributed endpoint (e.g. the line actually starting in Rajasthan). It is not: an independent, non-GEM, non-PNGRB source -- a GRIHA India (Green Rating for Integrated Habitat Assessment; India's own green-building certifier) case study PDF on the GAIL compressor-station administration building (https://www.grihaindia.org/sites/default/files/sites/default/files/pdf/case-studies/GAIL-Chainsa.pdf) -- states plainly 'Location: Chhainsa, Faridabad, Haryana' for the GAIL compressor station (same url_verifier PDF false-negative as above; confirmed manually via pdftotext, which pulled the location line cleanly). Faridabad is squarely in Haryana, not Rajasthan, so GEM's StartLocation=Chainsa/StartState=Haryana is correct, and Hissar is likewise a Haryana town, so EndState=Haryana is correct too. PNGRB's 'HR, RJ & DL' entry describes the route BETWEEN those two Haryana endpoints dipping through Rajasthan and Delhi (geographically plausible -- Faridabad sits on the Haryana/Delhi/Rajasthan tri-junction near the Bhiwadi-Neemrana industrial belt) -- a routing detail, not evidence the endpoints are wrong. This is a minor documentation gap (GEM's schema records endpoints only, not full transit-state lists), not an error, so I'm treating it as a caveat, not a concern.

validity.recommendation: Leave StartYear1=2023 as-is; it is plausible but not independently pinned to the exact year. Do NOT add a Diameter value -- the only lead found is too weak/ambiguous to stage.
validity.researcher_notes: StartYear1=2023: I could not find a source that states outright 'commissioned in 2023.' What I found instead triangulates loosely around it: the 2016 PNGRB report shows the line only 265/455 km built (41% short); by mid-2024 Indian Infrastructure reports it 'operating at 48 per cent capacity utilisation' (i.e. flowing gas, but well under nameplate); the current (May 2026) PNGRB report shows it 440/455 km 'operating' length under the fully-OPERATIONAL section, no length still tagged 'under construction.' A market database, offshore-technology.com (https://www.offshore-technology.com/marketdata/sultanpur-jhajjhar-hissar-gas-pipeline-india/, url_verifier OK on 'Sultanpur'), describes a '135km-long Sultanpur-Jhajjhar-Hissar' segment 'expected to commence operations in 2022' as part of a 'larger 304km Chainsa-Jhajjhar-Hissar system' -- a rough, one-year-off match to GEM's 2023, but I am NOT proposing it as a ref: (a) it names a different segment ('Sultanpur-Jhajjhar-Hissar', not the pipeline's GEM name), and (b) its '304km' total system length flatly conflicts with PNGRB's 455 km authorised length (confirmed identically in two PNGRB editions ten years apart) -- since this vendor database is already wrong on the one figure I can check against a primary regulator, I don't trust its 2022 completion date enough to stage it either, not even at low tier. Net: StartYear1=2023 is a reasonable estimate of when construction crossed some completion threshold, sits within the plausible window bounded by 2016 (41% built) and 2026 (97% built), but is not independently confirmed to the year -- flagging as an unresolved caveat rather than passing it silently. DIAMETER (a known India-gas gap per the orchestrator's guidance): the same offshore-technology.com page gives 'Maximum Diameter: 12 inches' for the Sultanpur-Jhajjhar-Hissar segment -- the only diameter lead I found for this pipeline -- but for the reasons above (wrong segment name, and the source's own length figure already conflicts with the regulator) I am not confident this 12in applies to the full 455 km trunk GEM records under P0912, so I am leaving Diameter blank rather than staging a number I can't stand behind.

summary: P0912 confirmed real and correctly classified/attributed (HIGH tier via PNGRB regulator, two editions 10 years apart, + independent Indian Infrastructure + GRIHA sources); two caveats flagged (not concerns): PNGRB's own register shows the route transiting Rajasthan/Delhi beyond GEM's Haryana-only endpoint fields, and StartYear1=2023 plus a possible Diameter=12in lead are both left unresolved as too weak/ambiguous to stage.
